Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our vendor security questionnaire (sensitive) — it's the canonical form our procurement team uses. We're most concerned about:

Hi Samantha

Appreciate the questionnaire — we've started a first pass. High-level answers to your four bullets while we go through the full form: 

- Admin activity logs: yes — we log user/admin identity changes, role grants/revocations, config changes, policy changes, and console actions. Every entry includes UTC timestamp, internal user id, external identity (if available), action, and source IP.

- API logs: we capture metadata (method, endpoint, status, latency) and payload hashes by default. For customers with strict needs we can capture request/response bodies behind customer-controlled encryption keys (Private and Dedicated setups) and for Hosted we provide redaction controls and hashed payload traces.

- Exportability: automated daily exports to customer S3, BigQuery, or secure FTP are supported. Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest. You can also run ad-hoc exports for arbitrary time windows.

- Immutability: for Hosted we provide append-only, versioned storage and 90-day immutable retention by default. For 7-year immutability and WORM (write-once-read-many) guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where logs can be written to customer-controlled immutable buckets (S3 Object Lock / retention policies) and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key control.

Next steps:
- We'll finish the questionnaire pass by end of day Thu (2027-06-22) and upload answers to the HubSpot deal record.
- Aditya, can you confirm the steps for setting up S3 exports with Object Lock for customers on Dedicated/Private?
- Samantha, if you can confirm whether Acme requires us to host immutable logs within your AWS account (preferred) or whether a Redwood-managed immutable archive is acceptable, we'll include the exact flow in our answers.

Sharing the SOC 2 summary and the audit-logging matrix (attached) — the matrix maps features/controls to typical regulatory asks.

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi Samantha

Quick technical details on the S3 export + immutability options Marissa mentioned: 

1) Customer-controlled S3 with Object Lock (recommended for 7-year retention):
   - Redwood writes daily batched log archives to a customer-provided S3 bucket.
   - Bucket must have Object Lock enabled and a retention policy configured; Redwood will respect the retention and cannot overwrite/delete locked objects.
   - We sign all objects with the customer's KMS key if provided, otherwise we can use a customer-managed key in your AWS account.

2) Redwood-managed immutable archive (alternative):
   - We can store immutable snapshots in our own archive layer for customers on Dedicated/Private if contractual terms include specific guarantees. This option requires a legal addendum.

3) API payloads: for Hosted customers we redacted PII by default; for Dedicated/Private we can store full payloads encrypted under your KMS and include those in exports.

Action items:
- Marissa: I'll post the technical export how-to (S3 params + IAM policy) to the HubSpot deal record and link to the KB.
- Samantha: if you can confirm your preference (customer S3 with Object Lock vs Redwood-managed archive) we'll include the exact implementation steps in the questionnaire answers.
- If helpful, propose we schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive this Wed or Thu (PST). I can demo a sample export and show how retention/immutability are enforced.

Thanks,
Aditya
